question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes self-pollination from cross-pollination in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
In self-pollination, pollen is transferred between different flowers of the same plant; in cross-pollination, pollen is transferred within the same flower.

(2)
In self-pollination, pollen from the same flower fertilizes the ovules; in cross-pollination, pollen is transferred between different flowers.

(3)
Self-pollination requires animal vectors while cross-pollination relies solely on wind.

(4)
There is no difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination.

explanation:
Self-pollination occurs when pollen from a flower fertilizes its own ovules, whereas cross-pollination
              involves pollen transfer between different flowers, promoting genetic variation.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following best defines sexual reproduction in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Production of offspring by vegetative means

(2)
Formation of new individuals through fusion of male and female gametes

(3)
A process involving only mitosis

(4)
Development of seeds without fertilization

explanation:
Sexual reproduction in flowering plants involves the fusion of male (pollen) and female (ovule) gametes,
              resulting in genetic recombination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Fertilization in flowering plants involves the fusion of which cells?

options.text:
(1)
Pollen grain and ovule

(2)
Sperm and egg cells

(3)
Pollen tube and ovule

(4)
Ovule and seed coat

explanation: Fertilization is the process in which a sperm cell fuses with an egg cell to form a zygote.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following best describes the function of the style in a flower?

options.text:
(1)
It produces pollen grains.

(2)
It serves as a pathway for the pollen tube to reach the ovary.

(3)
It develops into the fruit after fertilization.

(4)
It secretes nectar to attract pollinators.

explanation:
The style connects the stigma and ovary and provides a passageway for the pollen tube to deliver sperm
              cells to the ovule.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about self-incompatibility is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Self-incompatibility prevents self-fertilization and promotes cross-pollination.

(2)
Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism to avoid inbreeding.

(3)
Self-incompatibility allows pollen from the same plant to fertilize its ovules.

(4)
Self-incompatibility is controlled by S-genes.

explanation:
Self-incompatibility is a mechanism that prevents self-fertilization; it does not allow pollen from the
              same plant to fertilize its ovules.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about bat pollination is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Bat-pollinated flowers are typically large, pale or white, open at night, and emit a strong fruity or musky odor.

(2)
Bat-pollinated flowers are small, brightly colored, and open during the day.

(3)
Bat pollination relies exclusively on wind for pollen dispersal.

(4)
Bat-pollinated flowers have no nectar to reward pollinators.

explanation:
Bat-pollinated (chiropterophilous) flowers are generally large, pale-colored, and open at night, with a
              strong odor to attract bats.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding pollinator specificity and reproductive isolation is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Specialized pollinator interactions can contribute to reproductive isolation, thereby facilitating speciation in flowering plants.

(2)
Pollinator specificity has no effect on plant speciation.

(3)
Generalist pollination always leads to complete reproductive isolation.

(4)
Reproductive isolation is solely determined by geographic separation, independent of pollinator behavior.

explanation:
Specialized interactions between flowers and their pollinators can reinforce reproductive isolation by
              limiting gene flow between populations, thus promoting speciation.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: During megasporogenesis, how many megaspores are typically produced and how many usually survive?

options.text:
(1)
Four produced, one survives.

(2)
Four produced, two survive.

(3)
Eight produced, one survives.

(4)
Eight produced, four survive.

Meiosis produces a tetrad of megaspores, but typically only one functional megaspore survives while the
              others degenerate.

source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Cleistogamy is best described as:

Pollination by wind

Cross-pollination between different plants

Self-pollination occurring in unopened, closed flowers

Pollination mediated by water currents

question_text: Which of the following statements about nectaries is correct?

Nectaries produce pollen grains.

Nectaries secrete nectar to attract pollinators.

Nectaries are part of the male reproductive system.

Pollen tube

Style

Sepal

Petal

Small, green, and inconspicuous flowers with exposed stamens

Tubular shape with nectar guides

Dense clustering of showy petals

They remain closed during pollination

They exhibit self-pollination

They produce large, showy petals

They ensure reproduction under unfavorable conditions

source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about apomixis in flowering plants is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Apomixis is a sexual process involving the fusion of gametes.

(2)
Apomixis results in seed formation without fertilization, producing clonal offspring.

(3)
Apomixis is exclusive to gymnosperms.

Apomixis increases genetic variation through recombination.

question_text: Which of the following statements about auxin's role in fruit set is correct?

Auxin plays a crucial role in initiating fruit development after fertilization.

Auxin completely inhibits fruit growth.

(3)
Auxin is not involved in the process of fruit set.

Auxin only affects vegetative growth and not reproductive development.

subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about polyspermy prevention in flowering plants is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Mechanisms exist that ensure only one sperm fuses with the egg cell, thereby preventing polyspermy.

(2)
Polyspermy is common and beneficial in flowering plants.

(3)
Multiple sperm typically fuse with the egg cell to increase genetic diversity.

(4)
There is no mechanism to prevent polyspermy in angiosperms.

subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: What does the term 'gametophyte' refer to in flowering plants?

The generation that produces gametes

The tissue that gives rise to the fruit

The dormant stage of the embryo

source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following correctly defines herkogamy?

Temporal separation of male and female functions

Spatial separation of stamens and pistils within the flower

A genetic mechanism preventing self-fertilization

Transfer of pollen by wind

source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 2

The production of gametes

The fusion of male and female gametes

The process of seed dispersal

Ovary

Produce ovules

Serve as an entry point for the pollen tube

Develop into the seed coat

Attract pollinators

question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of entomophilous (insect-pollinated) flowers?

Reduced, greenish petals

Brightly colored and scented petals

Exposed stamens and pistils without nectar

question_text: Which of the following best explains the evolutionary significance of sexual reproduction in flowering plants?

It results in offspring that are genetically identical to the parent.

It generates genetic variability, enhancing adaptability to changing environments.

It reduces the chance of mutation.

It eliminates the need for pollinators.

question_text: Which of the following statements about the evolution of sexual reproduction in flowering plants is incorrect?

Sexual reproduction increases genetic diversity among offspring.

Sexual reproduction allows plants to adapt to changing environments.

(3)
Sexual reproduction always produces genetically identical offspring.

Sexual reproduction has contributed to the evolutionary success of angiosperms.

Synergid cells secrete chemical attractants to guide the pollen tube towards the embryo sac.

Synergid cells fuse with sperm cells to form the zygote.

It increases genetic variation, enhancing adaptability

Floral traits remain unchanged over evolutionary time.

Floral traits have no impact on the efficiency of pollination.

Floral traits are solely determined by genetic drift.

The zygote immediately develops into a mature embryo without any cell division.

Multiple zygotes fuse together to form a single embryo.

It does not involve the formation of endosperm.

explanation:
In double fertilization, one sperm fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, and the other fuses with
              the two polar nuclei to form a triploid endosperm.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements comparing sexual and asexual reproduction in flowering plants is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sexual reproduction, through processes like double fertilization, increases genetic recombination and diversity among offspring.

(2)
Asexual reproduction produces greater genetic variation than sexual reproduction.

(3)
Sexual reproduction results in genetically identical offspring.

(4)
Asexual reproduction always involves the fusion of gametes.

explanation:
Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of gametes and subsequent genetic recombination, which results in
              increased genetic diversity compared to asexual reproduction.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following is the most common type of embryo sac found in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Oenothera type

(2)
Allium type

(3)
Polygonum type

(4)
Drusa type

explanation:
The Polygonum type embryo sac is the most common type in angiosperms, typically having seven cells and
              eight nuclei.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about the structure of a mature pollen grain is correct?

options.text:
(1)
A mature pollen grain contains one vegetative cell and one generative cell (or two sperm cells, if the generative cell divides) depending on the species.

(2)
A mature pollen grain contains three vegetative cells.

(3)
A mature pollen grain contains no generative cells.

(4)
A mature pollen grain always contains only a single cell.

explanation:
A mature pollen grain typically comprises one vegetative cell and one generative cell; in many species,
              the generative cell divides to form two sperm cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about the genetic basis of self-incompatibility is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Self-incompatibility is governed by multiple alleles at the S-locus, preventing self-fertilization.

(2)
Self-incompatibility is controlled by a single gene with no allelic variation.

(3)
Self-incompatibility operates independently of the plant’s genotype.

(4)
Self-incompatibility is only observed in asexual reproduction.

explanation:
Self-incompatibility is a genetically controlled mechanism, typically involving multiple alleles at the
              S-locus, which prevents self-fertilization and promotes cross-pollination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following best describes the role of antipodal cells in the embryo sac?

options.text:
(1)
They fuse with the sperm cell to form the zygote

(2)
They assist in nourishing the embryo sac before degenerating

(3)
They develop into the endosperm

(4)
They form the seed coat

explanation:
Antipodal cells are thought to help in nourishing the embryo sac and usually degenerate later in
              development.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: For wind-pollinated flowers, which environmental factor is most critical for effective pollen dispersal?

options.text:
(1)
Humidity

(2)
Wind speed

(3)
Soil moisture

(4)
Ambient light

explanation:
Wind speed is crucial in wind-pollinated (anemophilous) plants to carry pollen grains over distances for
              successful pollination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which statement best summarizes the process of double fertilization in angiosperms?

options.text:
(1)
Two sperm cells fuse with two egg cells to form twin zygotes

(2)
One sperm fuses with the egg forming a zygote, while the other fuses with two polar nuclei to form the endosperm

(3)
Both sperm cells fuse with the egg cell simultaneously

(4)
Fertilization occurs without the involvement of polar nuclei

explanation:
Double fertilization involves one sperm cell fusing with the egg to form the zygote and the other fusing
              with the two polar nuclei to produce the triploid endosperm.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about the role of calcium ions in pollen tube elongation is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Calcium ions are essential for regulating the growth and directional guidance of the pollen tube.

(2)
Calcium ions inhibit the growth of the pollen tube.

(3)
Calcium ions are only involved in seed germination.

(4)
Calcium ions are not found in the pollen tube.

explanation:
Calcium ions play a crucial role in pollen tube elongation by regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and
              signaling pathways that direct the tube's growth toward the ovule.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which factor is most likely to enhance cross-pollination in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Structural adaptation that prevents self-pollination

(2)
Production of clonal, genetically identical seeds

(3)
The absence of pollinator attraction mechanisms

(4)
High levels of self-compatibility

explanation:
Structural and biochemical adaptations that prevent self-pollination promote cross-pollination, thereby
              increasing genetic diversity.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Double fertilization in angiosperms results in the formation of:

options.text:
(1)
Two zygotes

(2)
A diploid zygote and a triploid endosperm

(3)
Two embryos

(4)
An embryo and a seed coat

explanation:
Double fertilization involves one sperm fusing with the egg to form a diploid zygote, and another sperm
              fusing with the two polar nuclei to form a triploid endosperm, which nourishes the developing embryo.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about seed development in monocots and dicots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
In monocots, the endosperm is typically persistent in the mature seed, whereas in dicots it is usually absorbed by the developing embryo.

(2)
In dicots, the endosperm is persistent, while in monocots it is absorbed by the embryo.

(3)
Both monocots and dicots always retain a large endosperm in the mature seed.

(4)
Neither monocots nor dicots develop an endosperm during seed development.

explanation:
Typically, monocot seeds (e.g., cereals) retain a substantial endosperm, whereas in dicots the endosperm
              is often consumed by the embryo during development.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: What is the primary role of nectar in many flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
To serve as the male gametophyte

(2)
To attract pollinators by providing a sugar-rich reward

(3)
To initiate seed germination

(4)
To develop into the fruit

explanation:
Nectar is produced by many flowers to attract pollinators such as insects and birds, which in turn assist
              in pollination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following is a false statement regarding self-compatibility in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Self-compatibility allows a flower to fertilize itself.

(2)
It promotes genetic diversity by encouraging cross-pollination.

(3)
Self-compatibility can lead to inbreeding depression.

(4)
Self-compatible plants can produce offspring without the need for cross-pollination.

explanation:
Self-compatibility means that a plant can self-fertilize. While it offers reproductive assurance, it does
              not promote genetic diversity; in fact, cross-pollination is needed for increased variability.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which process is the primary source of genetic variation in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Mitosis

(2)
Clonal propagation

(3)
Meiosis

(4)
Budding

explanation:
Meiosis during gametogenesis introduces genetic variation through recombination and independent
              assortment of chromosomes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which type of pollination involves transfer of pollen by wind?

options.text:
(1)
Zoophily

(2)
Entomophily

(3)
Anemophily

(4)
Hydrophily

explanation: Anemophily is pollination by wind, typical in many grasses and some trees.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding seed coat formation is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The seed coat is derived from the integuments of the ovule.

(2)
The seed coat originates from the nucellus.

(3)
The seed coat is formed by the fusion of the funiculus and chalaza.

(4)
The seed coat is a product of the embryo sac cells.

explanation: The integuments surrounding the ovule differentiate into the seed coat (testa) after fertilization.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: The process by which a microspore develops into a mature pollen grain is termed:

options.text:
(1)
Megagametogenesis

(2)
Microgametogenesis

(3)
Pollen tube elongation

(4)
Sporogenesis

explanation:
Microgametogenesis is the process in which the haploid microspore develops into the male gametophyte
              (pollen grain) through mitotic divisions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding fruit set is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Effective pollination leads to a higher fruit set, while inadequate pollination can result in fruit abortion.

(2)
Fruit set is solely determined by the size of the flower.

(3)
Fruit set is independent of pollination efficiency.

(4)
Fruit set occurs even in the absence of fertilization.

explanation:
Successful and effective pollination is essential for fruit set; inadequate pollination can cause the
              flower or ovary to abort.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about nutrient transport within the ovule is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The chalaza is the region in the ovule that facilitates nutrient transfer from the placenta to the developing ovule.

(2)
Nutrient transport in the ovule occurs solely through the funiculus.

(3)
Nutrient transport is not necessary for ovule development.

(4)
The integuments are responsible for nutrient transport to the embryo.

explanation:
The chalaza is the key region of the ovule where nutrient transfer occurs from the placenta, ensuring the
              developing ovule is supplied with essential nutrients.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which statement regarding pollen tube growth is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Pollen tube growth is guided by a gradient of calcium ions and chemical attractants secreted by synergid cells.

(2)
Pollen tube growth occurs randomly within the style.

(3)
Pollen tube growth is independent of the pollen grain’s hydration.

(4)
Pollen tube growth is inhibited by the presence of chemical attractants.

explanation:
Calcium ions and attractant peptides (like LURE) secreted by synergid cells guide the pollen tube toward
              the embryo sac.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: How many nuclei are present in the mature Polygonum type embryo sac?
explanation: The mature Polygonum type embryo sac contains 7 cells with a total of 8 nuclei.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: In hydrophilous pollination, pollen is primarily transferred by:

options.text:
(1)
Wind

(2)
Insects

(3)
Water currents

(4)
Birds

explanation:
Hydrophilous pollination occurs when water currents carry pollen, a mechanism seen in some aquatic
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which structure in the ovule develops into the seed coat after fertilization?

options.text:
(1)
Integuments

(2)
Nucellus

(3)
Funiculus

(4)
Chalaza

explanation: The integuments surrounding the ovule develop into the seed coat (testa) after fertilization.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which process leads to the formation of the embryo sac in flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Microsporogenesis

(2)
Megasporogenesis followed by megagametogenesis

(3)
Microgametogenesis

(4)
Apomixis

explanation:
The embryo sac is formed from a functional megaspore that develops through megasporogenesis and then
              undergoes mitotic divisions (megasporogenesis followed by megagametogenesis).
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about floral induction is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Florigen is the hypothesized hormone that triggers flowering in response to photoperiod.

(2)
Flowering in plants is independent of day length.

(3)
Florigen is produced in the roots and transported upward.

(4)
Photoperiodism has no effect on the timing of flowering.

explanation:
Florigen is a putative hormone produced in leaves under specific photoperiodic conditions that travels to
              the shoot apex to induce flowering.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about seed dispersal is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Seed dispersal mechanisms include wind, water, animals, and explosive dehiscence.

(2)
Seed dispersal occurs exclusively through animal ingestion.

(3)
Seed dispersal always prevents seed predation.

(4)
Seed dispersal is not important for plant population expansion.

explanation:
Plants employ various seed dispersal mechanisms—wind, water, animals, and explosive dehiscence—to ensure
              wide distribution and reduce competition among seedlings.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about the S-locus in self-incompatibility is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The S-locus contains multiple alleles that prevent self-pollen from fertilizing the ovule.

(2)
The S-locus is responsible for forming the seed coat.

(3)
The S-locus promotes self-fertilization.

(4)
The S-locus is active only during fruit ripening.

explanation:
The S-locus governs self-incompatibility through multiple alleles that enable the plant to recognize and
              reject self-pollen, thereby promoting cross-pollination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Parthenocarpy in fruit development refers to:

options.text:
(1)
Fruit development after normal fertilization

(2)
Fruit development without fertilization, resulting in seedless fruits

(3)
Formation of multiple fruits from one flower

(4)
Abnormal seed development within the fruit

explanation:
Parthenocarpy is the process in which fruits develop without fertilization, usually leading to seedless
              fruits.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about the timing of pollen dehiscence is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Pollen dehiscence is often synchronized with the period of stigma receptivity to maximize successful fertilization.

(2)
Pollen dehiscence occurs at random times, regardless of stigma receptivity.

(3)
Pollen dehiscence is independent of environmental cues such as humidity and temperature.

(4)
Pollen dehiscence always occurs only at night.

explanation:
Successful pollination often depends on the synchronization of pollen release with the receptive phase of
              the stigma, ensuring maximum chances of fertilization.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the function of antipodal cells is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Antipodal cells fuse with sperm cells to form the zygote.

(2)
Antipodal cells contribute to nutrient absorption in the embryo sac and typically degenerate later.

(3)
Antipodal cells develop into the endosperm.

(4)
Antipodal cells form the seed coat.

explanation:
Antipodal cells are part of the embryo sac and are thought to assist in nutrient absorption before they
              eventually degenerate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: A pollen grain containing one vegetative cell and one generative cell is described as:

options.text:
(1)
Unicellular

(2)
Bicellular

(3)
Tricellular

(4)
Multicellular

explanation:
Bicellular pollen grains contain one vegetative cell and one generative cell. The generative cell may
              later divide to form two sperm cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about nectar production is false?

options.text:
(1)
Nectar is produced to attract pollinators.

(2)
Nectar contains sugars and amino acids.

(3)
All flowers produce nectar regardless of their pollination mechanism.

(4)
Nectar rewards help facilitate cross-pollination.

explanation:
Not all flowers produce nectar; some, especially wind-pollinated species, do not rely on nectar to
              attract pollinators.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following is a feature of flowers that are adapted for water pollination (hydrophily)?

options.text:
(1)
Large, bright petals

(2)
Reduced or absent petals and stamens

(3)
Sticky surfaces to capture pollen

(4)
Fragrant nectar production

explanation:
Hydrophilous flowers often lack showy petals and have reduced reproductive organs because water itself
              facilitates pollen transfer.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about endosperm absorption in dicot seeds is correct?

options.text:
(1)
In many dicot seeds, the developing embryo absorbs most of the endosperm during embryogenesis, resulting in a mature seed with little or no endosperm.

(2)
Dicot seeds always retain a large endosperm as a storage tissue in the mature seed.

(3)
Endosperm absorption in dicots occurs after the seed germinates.

(4)
Dicot seeds do not develop an endosperm during double fertilization.

explanation:
In many dicots, the endosperm is largely consumed by the growing embryo during seed development, so the
              mature seed contains little to no endosperm.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about megasporogenesis is correct?

options.text:
(1)
During megasporogenesis, one functional megaspore is produced from the megaspore mother cell while the others degenerate.

(2)
Megasporogenesis produces multiple functional megaspores that fuse to form the embryo sac.

(3)
All megaspores formed during megasporogenesis develop into embryo sacs.

(4)
Megasporogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in the ovule.

explanation:
Typically, meiosis in the megaspore mother cell produces four megaspores, but only one survives to
              develop into the functional embryo sac.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: The chalaza in an ovule functions primarily to:

options.text:
(1)
Anchor the ovule to the placenta and facilitate nutrient transport

(2)
Form the seed coat

(3)
Develop into the embryo sac

(4)
Produce the funiculus

explanation:
The chalaza is the region where the integuments and nucellus meet; it plays a role in nutrient transfer
              from the placenta to the ovule.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following structures secretes chemical attractants (LURE peptides) to guide the pollen tube in the embryo sac?

options.text:
(1)
Egg cell

(2)
Synergid cells

(3)
Central cell

(4)
Antipodal cells

explanation:
Synergid cells in the embryo sac secrete LURE peptides that attract the pollen tube toward the egg
              apparatus.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which statement about pollen tube growth is true?

options.text:
(1)
Pollen tube growth is independent of external signals.

(2)
Pollen tubes grow randomly in the style.

(3)
Pollen tube growth is guided by chemical signals secreted by the embryo sac.

(4)
Pollen tubes only grow if the flower is self-compatible.

explanation:
Chemical attractants, such as LURE peptides from the synergid cells, guide the pollen tube to the embryo
              sac for successful fertilization.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about the function of the filament is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The filament supports the anther, ensuring its optimal position for pollen release.

(2)
The filament produces pollen grains.

(3)
The filament develops into the fruit after fertilization.

(4)
The filament secretes nectar to attract pollinators.

explanation: The filament serves to support the anther, positioning it so that pollen can be effectively dispersed.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about double fertilization is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Double fertilization involves the fusion of two sperm cells with two egg cells.

(2)
Double fertilization results in the formation of a zygote and a triploid endosperm.

(3)
Double fertilization occurs in both angiosperms and gymnosperms.

(4)
Double fertilization produces two embryos in one ovule.

explanation:
In double fertilization, one sperm cell fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, while the other
              fuses with the two polar nuclei to produce a triploid endosperm.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about self-pollination is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Self-pollination increases homozygosity and reduces genetic diversity among offspring.

(2)
Self-pollination results in high genetic variability among offspring.

(3)
Self-pollination always leads to hybrid vigor.

(4)
Self-pollination is solely determined by environmental factors.

explanation:
Self-pollination often leads to increased homozygosity, which can reduce genetic diversity and may
              increase susceptibility to inbreeding depression.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about the integuments of the ovule is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Integuments protect the ovule and later develop into the seed coat.

(2)
Integuments are responsible for forming the embryo sac.

(3)
Integuments attract pollinators.

(4)
Integuments fuse with the funiculus to form the fruit.

explanation:
The integuments surround and protect the ovule and eventually develop into the seed coat after
              fertilization.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which hormone is primarily responsible for fruit ripening in many flowering plants?

options.text:
(1)
Auxin

(2)
Cytokinin

(3)
Ethylene

(4)
Gibberellin

explanation: Ethylene is the key plant hormone that regulates and promotes fruit ripening in many species.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about the disadvantages of self-pollination is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Self-pollination can lead to inbreeding depression and reduced genetic diversity among offspring.

(2)
Self-pollination increases genetic variation.

(3)
Self-pollination always results in more vigorous offspring than cross-pollination.

(4)
Self-pollination eliminates the risk of inbreeding depression.

explanation:
Self-pollination tends to increase homozygosity, which can lead to inbreeding depression and a reduction
              in genetic diversity, making populations less adaptable.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Megagametogenesis is the process by which:

options.text:
(1)
Microspores form the pollen grain

(2)
The functional megaspore develops into the embryo sac

(3)
Two sperm cells are produced

(4)
The pollen tube emerges from the pollen grain

explanation:
Megagametogenesis is the process through which the surviving megaspore undergoes mitotic divisions to
              form the mature embryo sac (female gametophyte).
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants / Test 10
